The input supports strides, so output should be created with same shape and strides to preserve layout. For layer_norm, normalized_shape parameter in Python is the number of trailing dims (int). We'll use it to verify that normalized_shape equals 3? Actually contract says normalized_shape int is len(normalized_shape), so it's 3. We can check x.dim() >= normalized_shape and that trailing dims match? But .cu launcher expects 4D dims [N,C,H,W] and strides. We'll only support 4D as per contract. We'll set C,H,W from x size and N from x size(0). Check x.is_cuda, dtype float32. For abs, output = torch::empty_strided(x.sizes(), x.strides(), x.options()). For layer_norm, same. model_new.py calls cuda_extension.abs_forward(x) and cuda_extension.layer_norm_forward(x, len(self.normalized_shape), self.eps).
Operator contract requires parameters exactly: abs_forward has one tensor x; layer_norm_forward has tensor x, int normalized_shape, double eps.
Output must preserve shape, dtype, device, and strides to match reference torch.abs and F.layer_norm
No torch:: operators allowed; only torch::empty_strided for allocation.
